definition.meaning: net heat that crosses the boundary of the liquid fuel control volume from its surroundings, per unit time when written as a rate
definition.control_volume: liquid phase only, open system at constant pressure; feed enters as liquid, vapour leaves at the surface temperature

ledger_mapping.prescribed_heating: growth of liquid sensible storage only
ledger_mapping.double_counting_guard: heating the feed up to the surface temperature is inside the release cost and is not heating

sandia_2011.citation: Blanchat, T. K. and Suo-Anttila, J., Hydrocarbon Characterization Experiments in Fully Turbulent Fires - Results and Data Analysis, SAND2010-6377, Sandia National Laboratories, March 2011
sandia_2011.rights: cover: Approved for public release; further dissemination unlimited

hamins_1994.citation: Hamins, A., Fischer, S. J., Kashiwagi, T., Klassen, M. E. and Gore, J. P., Heat Feedback to the Fuel Surface in Pool Fires, Combustion Science and Technology 97, 37-62 (1994); NIST reprint
hamins_1994.rights: NIST cover says not subject to copyright; the scanned journal page carries a publisher notice. Not archived; a few numbers transcribed with locators

kim_2019.citation: Kim, S. C., Lee, K. Y. and Hamins, A., Energy Balance in Medium-Scale Methanol, Ethanol, and Acetone Pool Fires, Fire Safety Journal 107, 44-53 (2019); NIST author manuscript

criteria.fixed_from: uncertainties the sources themselves state; written before the auditor was run, after a hand estimate of the order of magnitude
criteria.strict_closure: abs(independent - demand) / demand <= root sum of squares of the stated gauge and mass uncertainties
criteria.loose_closure_origin: lower end of the 20 to 40 percent the Sandia report cites for heat flux gauges in fire applications
criteria.point_identifiability: strict closure in every run and every balance term measured or demonstrably null
criteria.interval_identifiability: loose closure in every run with every unmeasured term named
criteria.transient: requires synchronised time series of the independent input and of the liquid state; a steady mean never approves it

sandia_2m.fuel: n-heptane, listed as 100%Heptane; purity not stated
sandia_2m.ambient_pressure_note: Albuquerque, about 24.6 in. Hg; below the 100 kPa of the liquid profile

gauge.type: Schmidt-Boelter water-cooled thermopile, total heat flux
gauge.body_temperature: oil bath a few degrees above the measured boiling temperature; gauge about 10 degrees hotter than the bath

sandia_2m.surface_temperature_locator: Table 12 p.76, measured boiling temperature; Figure 56 p.73

uncertainty.gauge_locator: p.37-38: the uncertainty includes gauge, fuel/gauge temperature and reflectivity differences and the area integration; no combined figure is given
uncertainty.mass_rate_example_scope: stated for a JP8 test averaged over 6 min; not stated for the heptane windows of 2 to 5.5 min

sandia_2m.tests_locator: Table 1 p.22, Table 2 p.23, Table 5 p.33, Table 8 p.36; heptane rows checked on page images, not only on extracted text
source_discrepancies: Table 12 prints 193.3 g/s as the mean with beads; the two tests of Table 1 average 197.25 g/s, with the printed standard deviation
SNL030 has heat flux rows but no row in Tables 1 and 2: its burn rate is not printed and it stays out of the balance
Table 3 lists a handbook heat of gasification of 541 kJ/kg for heptane; it is not used here

term_status.gauge_heat_flux: measured, same run as the mass rate, time average over the valid window
term_status.area_integral: computed from a designed equal-area ring layout; no extrapolation
term_status.mass_rate: measured on the supply drum; equals the pool loss only as an average over fill cycles
term_status.surface_temperature: measured as a plateau of the liquid rake; one value for the fuel, not per test
term_status.feed_temperature: measured before ignition only; the steady feed temperature is not tabulated for heptane
term_status.surface_reflection: measured in the laboratory at room temperature, per wavelength and two angles; the hemispherical total is not tabulated
term_status.vapour_dome_absorption_below_the_gauge: unknown: spectra were measured but no integrated transmittance for the 26 mm below the gauge face is tabulated
term_status.liquid_storage_growth: unknown: no time series of the liquid temperature is tabulated for heptane
term_status.gauge_to_surface_convective_difference: unknown: named by the report, not quantified
term_status.surface_reradiation: modelled bound: the gauge runs near the surface temperature, so most of it is already in the reading
term_status.feed_enthalpy: calculated with the approved liquid profile from the temperature before ignition

nist_030m.surface_temperature_note: the paper assumes the boiling point; TN 2162r1 prints 65 C in Table 12 and na in Table 13. Neither is accepted: both are propagated. The upper value is the end of the approved liquid support
nist_030m.feed_temperature_note: not reported for heptane; cooling water at 289 K below, a laboratory at 296 K in the reflection measurement
nist_030m.gauge_profile: TN 2162r1 Table F38, already transcribed and hashed in the provenance record of 2026-10-04
nist_030m.channels_note: the gauge profile comes from the simple burner and the mass rate from the ring burners: same configuration, different runs, steady means only

term_status.gauge_heat_flux: measured with a gauge cooled with room-temperature water at the plane of the lip
term_status.mass_rate: measured in ring burners in other runs of the same configuration
term_status.burner_loss: measured by water calorimetry, published only as a ratio to a mass-derived quantity
term_status.storage_growth: calculated from liquid thermocouples, published only as a ratio; the series shown is for methanol
term_status.reradiation: modelled with unit emissivity at the assumed boiling point

nist_alcohols_030m.why_examined: the only archived family with tabulated liquid temperature series (TN 2162r1 Appendix G)
nist_alcohols_030m.rejected_for: no approved property profile for these fuels; its fuel-side balance also leaves burner losses, reradiation, reflection and storage in one unmeasured remainder
nist_alcohols_030m.fuel_side_statement: the gauge integral exceeds the heat needed to vaporise the measured mass by 22 to 40 percent for methanol and ethanol
nist_alcohols_030m.locator: equations 13-14 and the discussion of Figures 7 and 9 of the manuscript
